summary: The note compares employment trends in traditional retail and e-commerce as of late 2023, arguing that physical stores are evolving toward experiential formats while online retail expands remote and analytical jobs. It covers skill requirements, compensation, job security and community impact, citing various experts and reports. It concludes that online and offline will converge in omnichannel experiences, with versatile, tech-savvy workers best positioned.
one_line: Retail and e-commerce employment are diverging and converging in skills, pay, security and community impact, favoring versatile, tech-savvy workers.
key_facts: Retail consultant Michael Ford believes physical stores will evolve into more experiential places, raising demand for skills like in-store tech support and interactive salesmanship.
On October 8, 2023, Harrison & Co. unveiled a new flagship store concept in New York City with VR changing rooms and interactive product customization studios.
A November 2, 2023 report by the National Association of Online Retailers expects e-commerce to create 2 million new jobs in the next five years.
E-commerce roles include digital marketing specialists, data analysts, logistics managers and remote customer service representatives.
Jane Matthews, Shopfinity's Head of Global Talent Acquisition, said ecommerce jobs offer location independence, letting the company attract top talent without geographical constraints.
Retail sales associates may now need to manage in-store digital kiosks or process online pick-up orders.
IT recruiter Tyler Smith said on December 5, 2023 that e-commerce firms seek people who can use big data, manage AI-driven chatbots and optimize supply chains with software.

A Retail Compensation Analytics survey on October 15, 2023 found e-commerce roles offer higher starting salaries on average, but retailers are closing the gap with performance bonuses, staff discounts and in-house career advancement programs.
Retail Workers Union representative Lisa Gonzales said on September 20, 2023 that traditional retail roles increasingly offer competitive wages and benefits.
Traditional retail jobs are historically more prone to economic fluctuations and seasonal hiring surges and layoffs, such as around Black Friday and the holidays.
Economist Dr. Emily Tran said on November 30, 2023 that people need to shop for essentials regardless of downturns, supporting e-commerce job stability.
Mayor Sarah Bennett said on December 12, 2023 that a new distribution center brought jobs but doesn't replace the vibrancy of local retail jobs.
E-commerce employment concentrates in warehousing and distribution centers that can be geographically removed from the communities they serve.
